verdicts.reason: A: the whole text block is tiny for a 768 square (the 'London' headline is only about 1/5 of the width, and the italic tagline is barely readable). It floats in a narrow translucent band over a busy skyline, with large dead areas around it, so it reads as the skyscraper layout shrunk into the middle rather than a re-layout for the new shape. B: the type is larger and more readable and the hierarchy is clearer. But the cluster is pushed left of the translucent band, the '<<<' chevrons float far off to the right beside the skyline and are cut off from the text, and the tagline sits straight on busy buildings with weak contrast. Both lose the Tower Bridge imagery. B wins narrowly on legibility.
